subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a separate assistant action-token search path, and what containment rules should govern action-token capture, retention, redaction, scope, and coexistence with user-token `search.messages`?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested capability handles event-scoped Slack authorization and workspace-wide search results, so automation should not choose the permanent token/privacy contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with thread/user/account-bound action-token handling, no raw-token persistence or logging, docs, focused tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Consolidate Slack search first
options.body: Define one Slack search contract covering both RTS and user-token `search.messages`, then implement the chosen action surface once.

options.title: Defer workspace search
options.body: Keep Slack workspace search out of OpenClaw until maintainers are ready to own the token, privacy, scope, and validation burden.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with thread/user/account-bound action-token handling, no raw-token persistence or logging, docs, focused tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Slack assistant lifecycle, context preservation, action runtime, and action-parity history all route through this owner path.
